subject: Reasoning
description: Day-of-week problems, leap years, odd days, repeating calendars

questions.stem: How many ODD DAYS are there in a NON-LEAP year (365 days)?
questions.explanation: ODD DAYS = days ≡ remainder when total days mod 7. Non-leap year = 365 days; 365/7 = 52 weeks + 1 day → 1 ODD day. LEAP year = 366 = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. INSIGHT — calendar repeats every 7 days; tracking 'odd days' tells you which DAY OF WEEK shifts. After 1 non-leap year, day shifts by 1; after leap year by 2. Useful for: 'what day was X date?' problems. RULE: 100 years = 124 odd days = 124 mod 7 = 5 odd days. 400 years = 0 odd days (calendar repeats). LEAP YEAR rules: divisible by 4 (year divisible by 4 = leap); EXCEPT century years divisible by 100 (NOT leap) UNLESS also divisible by 400 (THEN leap). 2000 = leap (÷ 400). 1900 = NOT leap.

questions.stem: If 1 January 2025 is a Wednesday, what day will 1 January 2026 be?
questions.explanation: 2025 is NOT a leap year (not divisible by 4). So 1 odd day → next year same date shifts forward 1 weekday. Wed → Thu. SIMILARLY: 1 Jan 2027 (after 2026 — also non-leap) → Friday. 1 Jan 2028 (after 2027, non-leap) → Saturday. 1 Jan 2029 (after 2028 LEAP) → Monday (skips Sunday since 2 odd days). RULE: every non-leap shifts by 1; leap shifts by 2. INSIGHT — calendar fully repeats every 28 years (or 11/6 years for non-leap/leap-pair if no century year intervenes). Useful for: birthday-day questions, anniversary-day predictions.

questions.stem: Which of the following years is a LEAP YEAR?
questions.explanation: LEAP YEAR rules: (1) Divisible by 4 → leap; (2) BUT if divisible by 100 → NOT leap; (3) EXCEPT divisible by 400 → leap. 2000: ÷ 400 → leap ✓. 1900: ÷ 100 (not 400) → NOT leap. 2023: not ÷ 4 → not leap. 1700: ÷ 100 (not 400) → not leap. INSIGHT — Gregorian calendar (introduced 1582 by Pope Gregory XIII) uses this rule to align with solar year (~365.2422 days). India adopted Gregorian 1752 (along with British Empire — that year 'lost' 11 days, Sept 3-13 simply didn't exist!). Earlier JULIAN calendar (Julius Caesar's) had simpler 'every 4 years leap' → drifted ~11 min/year → reached 11 days off by 1582. Hence Gregorian fix. Russia kept Julian till 1918; Greece till 1923.

questions.stem: If 14 August is a Monday, what day will be 14 OCTOBER (same year)?
questions.explanation: Days from 14 Aug to 14 Oct: AUG remaining (Aug 14 to Aug 31) = 17; SEP = 30; OCT 14 = 14. Total = 17 + 30 + 14 = 61 days. (Easier: count 31 (Aug 14 to Sep 14) + 30 (Sep 14 to Oct 14) = 61 — both methods.) 61 mod 7 = 5 odd days. So Mon + 5 = Sat. INSIGHT — count days INCLUDING start or NOT carefully (here 'from Aug 14 TO Oct 14' = 61 days difference; or '61 days later'). Practical use: planning meetings, calculating EMI / interest dates, SQL date arithmetic.

questions.stem: How many days are there in a leap year (Feb has 29)?
questions.explanation: LEAP year: 366 days (29 days in February). NORMAL year: 365 (28 in Feb). EXTRA day INSERTED to align CIVIL CALENDAR with TROPICAL year (Earth's orbital period ~365.2422 days). Without leap: drift of ~6 hours/year → ~24 days/century. WHY 29 FEB? Roman tradition; Feb was the SHORTEST month (since Caesar's time). LEAPLINGS = people born Feb 29 (rare, ~1 in 1500); celebrate birthday on 28 Feb / 1 Mar in non-leap years. Years with FEB 29: 2024, 2028, 2032, ..., 2100 NOT (century not by 400). FAMOUS LEAP YEAR EVENTS: 2020 (COVID-19 began), 2016 (Brexit, Trump won), 2012 (Mayan calendar end / Olympics in London), 2008 (Lehman crisis).

questions.stem: What was the day on 26 January 1950 (India became Republic)?
questions.explanation: 26 JAN 1950 = THURSDAY. INDIA's Constitution adopted; Republic Day. METHOD: count odd days from any reference; standard table-based approach: 1600 yrs (0 odd) + 300 yrs (1 odd × 3 = 3) + 49 yrs (49 + 12 leap = 61 odd → 5 odd) + January 26 = 26 odd. Total: 0 + 3 + 5 + 26 mod 7 = 34 mod 7 = 6 odd days = THURSDAY. (Mon=1, Tue=2, Wed=3, Thu=4, Fri=5, Sat=6, Sun=0; or by convention Sun=0/7, Mon=1, ...) PRACTICAL — Indian school problems require this for 26 Jan, 15 Aug, Gandhi Jayanti type dates. Sometimes you can use known anchors: 'I know Today is X day, and date Y... how many days difference + add'. Easier method.

questions.stem: After how many years does the SAME calendar (same day-date pairing) typically repeat for a non-leap year?
questions.explanation: FOR NON-LEAP year: same calendar can repeat in 6 OR 11 years (depending on placement of leap years between). E.g., 2025 calendar = 2031 calendar (next match), then 2042. FOR LEAP year: typically repeats every 28 years (cycle of 4 leap years × 7 days). Special case: when a CENTURY YEAR intervenes (like 1900, 2100 — non-leap centuries) — disrupts pattern. KEY: cumulative odd days must reset to 0 (mod 7). Each non-leap = 1 odd day; each leap = 2 odd days. Sum must be 0 (mod 7) for calendar repeat. PRACTICAL — 'same desk calendar can be reused after X years' calculations. INSIGHT — every year-month-day combo cycles every 400 years guaranteed (Gregorian cycle).
